question: A topical antifungal cream applied to the scalp is sufficient to cure tinea capitis in children.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Topical antifungals cannot penetrate the hair shaft where the dermatophyte resides in tinea capitis. Systemic therapy (oral griseofulvin or terbinafine) is mandatory for cure. Relying on topical cream alone leads to treatment failure and risks scarring alopecia from persistent infection.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. Tinea capitis involves the hair shaft, which topical agents cannot adequately penetrate. Systemic therapy is mandatory — oral griseofulvin (especially effective for Microsporum species) or oral terbinafine (preferred for Trichophyton species) — usually with an adjunct antifungal shampoo to reduce spore shedding and transmission.
